gaps.sentence: We ___ a taxi from the airport because it was raining.
gaps.explanation: take a taxi/bus/train is the standard collocation for using transport.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ the washing-up in your house?
gaps.explanation: do the washing-up means to wash the dishes; the -s form is needed with 'who'.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: The poster in the shop window ___ my eye.
gaps.explanation: catch somebody's eye means to attract someone's attention.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.
